name: Question 4
problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 7 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $a,$ $b,$ $c,$ and  $d:$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 7 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M:$

$$
V=|det(M)|
$$

Notice that the $4$th row of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 7 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1\cdot (-1)^{4+2}|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =-|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 1 \\  & =-12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V=|det(M)|=|-12|=12.
$$

EXPLANATION

First, let's construct the matrix M, whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors a, b, c, and d:

M=[4500−57302−2210−100]

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of M:

V=|det(M)|

Notice that the 4th row of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the 4th row, we have

det(M)=|4500−57302−2210−100|=−1⋅(−1)4+2|400−530221|=−|400−530221|.

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

det(M)=−|400−530221|=−1⋅4⋅3⋅1=−12

Therefore, the volume is

V=|det(M)|=|−12|=12.
